tactics.name: Reconnaissance
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gather information they can use to plan future operations.

tactics.name: Resource Development
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to establish resources they can use to support operations.

tactics.name: Initial Access
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to get into your network via entry vectors like phishing, exploit public-facing apps, or valid accounts.

tactics.name: Execution
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to run malicious code via command interpreters, scripts, or APIs.

tactics.name: Persistence
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to maintain their foothold across restarts and credential changes.

tactics.name: Privilege Escalation
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gain higher-level permissions like SYSTEM, root, or domain admin.

tactics.name: Defense Evasion
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to avoid being detected by obfuscation, process injection, or disabling security tools.

tactics.name: Credential Access
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to steal account names and passwords via dumping, sniffing, or keylogging.

tactics.name: Discovery
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to figure out your environment, system info, network topology, and accounts.

tactics.name: Lateral Movement
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to move through your environment using remote services, SMB, or SSH.

tactics.name: Collection
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gather data of interest like documents, emails, or keystrokes.

tactics.name: Command and Control
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to communicate with compromised systems to control them.

tactics.name: Exfiltration
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to steal data via encrypted channels, cloud storage, or alternate protocols.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to manipulate, interrupt, or destroy your systems and data (e.g. ransomware).

T1059.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
T1059.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.
T1059.detection: Monitor process execution logs, command line arguments, and parent-child process anomalies.
mitigations: Disable unnecessary scripting engines
Enforce code signing policies
Use application control like AppLocker / WDAC

T1059.001.name: PowerShell
T1059.001.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful interactive command-line interface and scripting environment.
T1059.001.detection: Enable Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104), Module Logging (4103), and Transcription. Monitor for encoded command flags (-enc, -encodedcommand) and unconstrained download cradles.
mitigations: Enable PowerShell Constrained Language Mode
Configure AppLocker to restrict script execution
Monitor and alert on unusual encoded command executions

T1059.003.name: Windows Command Shell
T1059.003.description: Adversaries may abuse cmd.exe to execute commands or batch files.
T1059.003.detection: Monitor process creation events (Event ID 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1) for suspicious cmd.exe flags and pipe operations.
mitigations: Disable cmd.exe execution for unprivileged accounts where not needed
Audit command lines

T1059.005.name: Visual Basic
T1059.005.description: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic (VBScript / VBA) for execution via malicious Office documents or WScript/CScript.
T1059.005.detection: Monitor Office applications spawning wscript.exe, cscript.exe, or powershell.exe.
mitigations: Block macros in Office files downloaded from the internet
Enforce ASR rules

T1547.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
T1547.description: Adversaries may configure system settings to automatically execute a program during system boot or logon.
T1547.detection: Monitor registry modifications to Run / RunOnce keys, Startup folder additions, and service installations.
mitigations: Restrict write access to autorun registry keys and startup folders
Regularly audit startup entries with Sysinternals Autoruns

T1547.001.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
T1547.001.description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding an entry to the 'Run' or 'RunOnce' keys in the Windows Registry or adding files to the Startup folder.
T1547.001.detection: Monitor Sysmon Event 13 (Registry value set) targeting HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run or HKLM\...\CurrentVersion\Run.
mitigations: Restrict unprivileged user modification of system-level registry keys
Use EDR auto-quarantine for unknown startup executables

T1053.name: Scheduled Task/Job
T1053.description: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling functionality to facilitate initial or recurring execution of malicious code.
T1053.detection: Monitor schtasks.exe and at.exe process execution, Windows Security Event ID 4698 (A scheduled task was created).
mitigations: Limit task creation privileges
Audit scheduled tasks on critical endpoints

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task
T1053.005.description: Adversaries may use the Windows Task Scheduler to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence.
T1053.005.detection: Monitor TaskScheduler operational logs (Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational) and schtasks /create commands.
mitigations: Enforce least privilege on Task Scheduler
Monitor XML task definitions under System32\Tasks

T1027.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
T1027.description: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, compressing, or XOR-masking content.
T1027.detection: Look for high Shannon entropy in file sections, encrypted resource payloads, and Base64/XOR decryption loops in memory.
mitigations: Deploy anti-malware with memory scanning and dynamic emulation capabilities
Block unapproved packers

T1027.002.name: Software Packing
T1027.002.description: Adversaries may compress or encrypt executables with custom packers or protectors (e.g. UPX, Themida, VMProtect) to hinder signature-based detection.
T1027.002.detection: Scan PE headers for abnormal section names and entropy signatures.
mitigations: Use file integrity monitoring and behavioral sandboxing

T1055.name: Process Injection
T1055.description: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.
T1055.detection: Monitor API calls like VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, and CreateRemoteThread via Sysmon Event 8 (CreateRemoteThread) or EDR API hooks.
mitigations: Enable Windows Defender Exploit Guard (Attack Surface Reduction)
Utilize Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) with kernel-level memory monitoring

T1055.001.name: Dynamic-link Library Injection
T1055.001.description: Adversaries may inject dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) into processes to evade defenses and execute arbitrary code.
T1055.001.detection: Monitor LoadLibrary calls in suspicious processes and Sysmon Event 7 (Image loaded).
mitigations: Enforce signed DLL loading policies via AppLocker / WDAC

T1055.012.name: Process Hollowing
T1055.012.description: Adversaries may inject malicious code into suspended legitimate processes by unmapping memory and rewriting entrypoints.
T1055.012.detection: Detect discrepancies between the PE file on disk and the loaded executable code in memory (NtUnmapViewOfSection).
mitigations: Deploy memory analysis tools like Volatility or modern EDR with memory integrity checks

T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol
T1071.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols (e.g., HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) to blend in with existing network traffic.
T1071.detection: Analyze TLS/SSL certificates, HTTP User-Agent anomalies, request frequency (jitter/beaconing), and POST body sizes.
mitigations: Perform SSL/TLS inspection on web proxies
Block known malicious domains and IP reputations

T1071.001.name: Web Protocols
T1071.001.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer web protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, WebSockets) to blend with normal web traffic.
T1071.001.detection: Detect periodic beaconing behaviors, rare user-agents, non-standard HTTP headers, or dynamic DNS domains.
mitigations: Enforce web proxies with SSL inspection
Employ threat intel domain blocklists

T1071.004.name: DNS
T1071.004.description: Adversaries may communicate using the Domain Name System (DNS) protocol for command and control or data exfiltration (DNS tunneling).
T1071.004.detection: Monitor high volumes of DNS queries with high entropy subdomains and non-standard record types (TXT, NULL).
mitigations: Filter external DNS traffic through internal recursive DNS resolvers with query logging and threat blocking

T1003.name: OS Credential Dumping
T1003.description: Adversaries may dump credentials from the operating system to obtain account login and credential material (e.g. LSASS memory, SAM database).
T1003.detection: Monitor access to lsass.exe process memory (Sysmon Event 10), invocations of MiniDumpWriteDump, and volume shadow copy access.
mitigations: Enable Credential Guard in Windows 10/11 and Server
Restrict debug privileges (SeDebugPrivilege)
Enable LSA Protection (RunAsPPL)

T1003.001.name: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.description: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS).
T1003.001.detection: Detect Mimikatz, procdump.exe, or comsvcs.dll dumping LSASS memory handles.
mitigations: Configure LSA Protection (RunAsPPL)
Enable Windows Defender Credential Guard

T1082.name: System Information Discovery
T1082.description: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware, including version, patches, and architecture.
T1082.detection: Monitor execution of systeminfo.exe, hostname, uname -a, and WMI queries for Win32_OperatingSystem.
mitigations: Restrict command execution for unprivileged accounts where possible
Audit discovery command telemetry

T1083.name: File and Directory Discovery
T1083.description: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or search in specific locations of a host to identify sensitive data or system files.
T1083.detection: Monitor dir, ls, findstr, or tree commands executed in rapid sequence by anomalous parent processes.
mitigations: Restrict access to sensitive file shares with proper ACLs
Audit file system access

T1046.name: Network Service Discovery
T1046.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts or local network segments (port scanning).
T1046.detection: Monitor rapid SYN/connect scans from single hosts across multiple internal IP subnets.
mitigations: Deploy internal network segmentation and firewalling
Alert on anomalous port scans

T1021.name: Remote Services
T1021.description: Adversaries may use valid credentials to log into a service that is designed to accept remote connections (e.g. RDP, SMB, SSH, WinRM).
T1021.detection: Monitor Windows Security Event ID 4624 (Logon Type 10 - RemoteInteractive or Type 3 - Network) and port 3389 / 445 / 5985 traffic.
mitigations: Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA)
Disable remote desktop or restrict RDP access via jump boxes

T1021.001.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
T1021.001.description: Adversaries may connect to remote systems via RDP to interact with user sessions and move laterally.
T1021.001.detection: Monitor RDP connection events,mstsc.exe executions, and unexpected internal RDP sessions.
mitigations: Enforce Network Level Authentication (NLA)
Use MFA for RDP access
Restrict port 3389 via host firewalls

T1021.002.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.description: Adversaries may use SMB to interact with administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) for lateral movement.
T1021.002.detection: Monitor Event ID 5140 (A network share object was accessed) and SMB PsExec-style service creation.
mitigations: Disable SMBv1
Block inbound SMB port 445 between internal workstation subnets

T1486.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
T1486.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt the availability of system and network resources (Ransomware).
T1486.detection: Detect rapid file modification/renaming rates, vssadmin delete shadows commands, and high I/O volume with new file extensions.
mitigations: Maintain immutable, offline backups
Protect Volume Shadow Copies
Deploy anti-ransomware behavioral blockers

T1490.name: Inhibit System Recovery
T1490.description: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in data recovery features, such as Volume Shadow Copies, backup catalogs, or system restore points.
T1490.detection: Monitor execution of vssadmin.exe delete shadows, bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No, and wbadmin.exe delete catalog.
mitigations: Restrict administrator execution of vssadmin and bcdedit commands
Enforce EDR blocking on recovery disabling commands

T1566.name: Phishing
T1566.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems via malicious attachments or links.
T1566.detection: Analyze email gateway telemetry, anomalous SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures, and macro-enabled attachments.
mitigations: Deploy email security gateway (SEG) with attachment sandboxing
Conduct regular security awareness training

T1566.001.name: Spearphishing Attachment
T1566.001.description: Adversaries may send targeted emails with malicious attachments (e.g. ISO, LNK, Office macros, ZIPs) to gain access.
T1566.001.detection: Inspect inbound email attachments with deep file inspection and sandbox detonation.
mitigations: Block dangerous attachment extensions at email gateway (.iso, .vbs, .hta, .exe, .scr)

T1190.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
T1190.description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a vulnerability in an Internet-facing computer or program to gain access.
T1190.detection: Monitor web server error logs (500s), WAF blocked requests, and suspicious child processes spawned by web server daemons (w3wp.exe, nginx, apache).
mitigations: Patch external systems promptly
Deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF)
Isolate public-facing DMZ servers

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, or Privilege Escalation.
T1078.detection: Detect impossible travel logins, unusual login times, and access to resources outside normal job roles.
mitigations: Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA)
Implement conditional access policies and continuous access evaluation

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
T1041.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.
T1041.detection: Monitor spikes in outbound data transfer volumes during C2 sessions.
mitigations: Implement data loss prevention (DLP) and strict outbound network egress filtering

T1567.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
T1567.description: Adversaries may use legitimate external cloud storage or file-sharing services (e.g., Mega, Google Drive, OneDrive, Discord) to exfiltrate data.
T1567.detection: Monitor outbound upload requests to cloud storage URLs from unexpected processes.
mitigations: Implement Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB)
Block unapproved cloud file-sharing services

T1056.name: Input Capture
T1056.description: Adversaries may use methods of capturing user input to obtain credentials or sensitive information (e.g. Keylogging, GUI input capture).
T1056.detection: Monitor API hooks on SetWindowsHookEx, GetAsyncKeyState, and access to raw input devices.
mitigations: Use virtual keyboards or password managers
Deploy endpoint security with keystroke protection
